_comment: What grows in the Meadows playground, and where. ALL of it is TUNABLE. The expected feedback is 'too sparse', 'too busy', 'the trees are on the cliffs' — every one of those has to be answerable here rather than in a scene.
_comment_authored: This dresses the M1 MOVEMENT PLAYGROUND, not the real Meadows. M7 authors the actual geography and its placement will be authored rather than scattered. The RULES survive that; the specific clump centres do not.
_comment_clumping: Every layer clusters. Evenly-spread props at uniform scale are the readable signature of generator output — the visual rubric names it — so each layer places clumps and scatters within them, leaving clearings between. `strays` fills the gaps so the clumps do not read as islands.

trees._comment: Broadleaf, in copses. The largest silhouette in the meadow and therefore the thing that gives distance a scale — without trees the hills could be any size.
trees._comment_clumping: Fewer, tighter, larger copses rather than more small ones. The critic read the previous tree band as 'one blob mesh, one green, one approximate scale, at near-regular spacing along the ridge' — 26 clumps of 9 spread over 512m is close enough to even that it reads as a distribution. Twelve dense copses with real gaps between them reads as somebody deciding where a wood goes.
trees._comment_slope: Trees stop well before the rocky rises. A tree growing out of a cliff face is the cheapest way to destroy the sense that a place was authored.
trees._comment_scale: A 3.2x spread inside one copse. Uniform prop scale is the other readable signature of generator output, and a wood with saplings and old trees in it is the difference between a grove and a stamp.
trees._comment_clear: The spawn pad stays clear. The player's first sight of the game should not be the inside of a tree.
trees._comment_base_scale: Kenney's models are authored around one unit. A tree at one unit is knee-high next to a 1.8m trainer, which makes every hill read as a mound. This is the per-layer correction; scale_min/max vary around it.

grove._comment: The second canopy tone. Same pack, warmer and lighter leaf, clumped separately so copses are not all one colour — the critic's note that the hero tree is 'a single flat-shaded polyhedron of one green' applies to the whole band, and two tones with overlapping copses is the cheapest thing that reads as depth in a treeline.

bushes._comment: The middle layer. Without something between grass height and tree height the ground reads as a lawn with poles on it.
bushes._comment_base_scale: Kenney's models are authored around one unit. A tree at one unit is knee-high next to a 1.8m trainer, which makes every hill read as a mound. This is the per-layer correction; scale_min/max vary around it.

grass._comment: Tufts, not a ground texture. These are what make the terrain read as a meadow rather than as a painted surface, and they are the layer whose density most separates these frames from the reference.
grass._comment_scale: Widened well past the old 0.7-1.6. The critic named uniform prop scale as one of the two readable signatures of generator output, and a 2.3x spread inside one layer is what a real meadow looks like at ground level.
grass._comment_base_scale: Kenney's models are authored around one unit. A tree at one unit is knee-high next to a 1.8m trainer, which makes every hill read as a mound. This is the per-layer correction; scale_min/max vary around it.
grass._comment_shadow: No shadow. Thousands of tufts each casting one overlap into a black carpet on terrain that does receive — measured at luminance 0.068 in the near field against 0.27-0.60 across the references. A blade's shadow is not information at this scale.
grass._comment_clearings: Walked straight through, so it cannot hide a creature or block a camera — the arena clearings do not apply. Stripping it left the spawn as forty metres of bare ground in the foreground of every survey frame.

drygrass._comment: The SAME Kenney tufts, tinted straw instead of green, in their own patches. Two hue families where there was one, from assets already in the build. The critic counted 2 hue families in the frames against 6 on the key art board and 3-5 across the Palworld references, and said the board's golds appear nowhere below the horizon; this is where the gold comes from. Palworld's own meadows are yellow-green rather than green, which is most of why they photograph warm.
drygrass._comment_retint: Per-layer override of the global map. Same material name, different colour, so one mesh family carries two palettes.
drygrass._comment_shadow: No shadow. Thousands of tufts each casting one overlap into a black carpet on terrain that does receive — measured at luminance 0.068 in the near field against 0.27-0.60 across the references. A blade's shadow is not information at this scale.
drygrass._comment_clearings: Walked straight through, so it cannot hide a creature or block a camera — the arena clearings do not apply. Stripping it left the spawn as forty metres of bare ground in the foreground of every survey frame.

flowers._comment: Colour accents, clustered hard. Wildflowers grow in patches; spread evenly they read as confetti.
flowers._comment_density: Roughly four times the previous count and nearly twice the size. Not a whim: the critic measured saturated non-green pixels below the horizon at 0.000%-0.035% of frame against a design brief that says 'wildflower meadows', and found ZERO in 03-rise-overlook out of 921,600 pixels. The flowers were already there — 944 of them — and were simply too small and too sparse to occupy a pixel at any distance. A colour accent nobody can see is not an accent.
flowers._comment_base_scale: Kenney's models are authored around one unit. A tree at one unit is knee-high next to a 1.8m trainer, which makes every hill read as a mound. This is the per-layer correction; scale_min/max vary around it.

rocks._comment: Rocks go where trees will not: they are the layer that makes the steep ground read as stone rather than as grass at an angle.
rocks._comment_slope: The only layer with a MINIMUM slope as well as a maximum, so boulders gather on the shoulders and rises where they belong instead of sitting on flat grass like dropped props.
rocks._comment_base_scale: Kenney's models are authored around one unit. A tree at one unit is knee-high next to a 1.8m trainer, which makes every hill read as a mound. This is the per-layer correction; scale_min/max vary around it.

deadfall._comment: Logs and mushrooms, near where trees are. Sparse on purpose: this layer is detail for the moments the player is standing still, and at any real density it becomes clutter.
deadfall._comment_base_scale: Kenney's models are authored around one unit. A tree at one unit is knee-high next to a 1.8m trainer, which makes every hill read as a mound. This is the per-layer correction; scale_min/max vary around it.

_comment_retint: Kenney's Nature Kit ships a bright teal-green palette (#73ecdc grass, #6fe5d5 leaves). It is cohesive with itself and wrong for this project: against our grass terrain it reads as cyan plastic, and the key art board is a warm olive/leaf palette. So every source material is remapped by NAME to data/config/palette.json. Retinting rather than re-sourcing keeps the models' silhouettes, which are good.
_comment_flower_saturation: The three flower colours are the most saturated things in the meadow on purpose, and they are pushed further than a real petal because they are three pixels across at any distance the player usually stands. They stay clear of the Team Tether oxblood, which is reserved for danger.
_comment_collision: Layers marked `collides` get real static collision. Two reasons, and the second is the urgent one: a tree you can walk through reads as a hologram, and — because the camera's SpringArm3D only stops at things with collision — a bush with none lets the camera end up INSIDE it. Two survey frames came back showing nothing but green because the camera was inside a bush during a fight. Grass and flowers must never collide; you walk through those.
_comment_clearings: Open ground kept clear of every layer. These match the wild pal spawn points in scripts/combat/encounter_director.gd, because a fight starts where a creature is standing and the arena is 11m across: without this, the trees are inside the arena and stand between the camera and the fight. The radius is arena radius plus margin.

clearings._why: peaceful pal, and the arena around it
aggressive pal, and the arena around it
